summary.text: Barbara Kahl, a Republican veterinarian and fourth-generation Oregonian, lost the November 3, 2026 election for Oregon's 1st Congressional District to Suzanne Bonamici.
She worked for about two decades in corporate accounting, finance and purchasing before becoming a veterinarian, and ran a mobile large-animal practice for nearly 20 years.

paragraphs.text: Barbara Kahl describes herself as a fourth-generation Oregonian who worked as a child to help pay for her school clothes, and she graduated from Hillsboro High School.
She spent about two decades in corporate accounting, finance and purchasing in the frozen food, utilities and high-tech sectors, including at Intel's Hillsboro campus from 1990 to 1997.

She earned a bachelor's degree from Oregon State University in 2001 and a doctorate in veterinary medicine from Oregon State's College of Veterinary Medicine in 2006, and says she attended college while raising a family.

Kahl describes herself as a USDA-APHIS nationally accredited veterinarian who spent nearly 20 years running a mobile practice serving large animals, equine, small animals, exotics and livestock across the district.
She says she founded the USPCA nonprofit and rescue organization and received the Oregon Veterinary Medical Association's 2012 Animal Welfare Award.

She serves as a public member of the Oregon Department of Agriculture's CAFO Advisory Committee and has testified before the Oregon Legislature on agriculture, veterinary practice and animal-welfare bills.

Kahl says she traveled with her husband during his military deployments, and the two live on farmland in rural Oregon. She won the May 19, 2026 Republican primary with 71.5% of the vote over John Verbeek.
Her campaign materials emphasized jobs and the economy, education, affordability and federal fiscal accountability.
She received 28.8% of the vote to Suzanne Bonamici's 71.0%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
